syllabus_version.title: CBSE Curriculum for the Academic Year 2026-27

topics.title: Lencho's hope for rain

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the setting of Lencho's house and explain why he was waiting eagerly for rain.
Interpret Lencho's comparison of raindrops to new coins and what it shows about his hopes.

topics.title: The hailstorm destroys the crop
topics.ncert_sections: The hailstorm and the sorrowful night

concepts.learning_objective: Recall how the rain turned into a hailstorm and describe the damage it caused.
Explain the conflict between humans and nature, and between humans themselves, in the story.

topics.title: Lencho's faith and his letter to God
topics.ncert_sections: Lencho writes and posts his letter

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the lines that show Lencho's complete faith in God.
Recall what Lencho asked for in his letter to God and why.

topics.title: The postmaster's act of goodwill
topics.ncert_sections: The post office reads and answers the letter

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why the postmaster answered the letter and signed it 'God'.
Recall how the postmaster gathered money for Lencho and how much he could send.

topics.title: Lencho's reply and the irony of the story
topics.ncert_sections: Lencho receives the money and writes again

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the irony in Lencho blaming the post office employees for the missing money.
Evaluate Lencho's character using evidence from the story.

topics.title: Grammar: relative clauses, negatives for emphasis and 'hope'

concepts.learning_objective: Identify non-defining relative clauses and join sentences using who, whom, whose and which.
Distinguish negatives that show absence from negatives used for emphasis.
Distinguish the uses of 'hope' as a noun and as a verb.

topics.title: Metaphors and storm vocabulary
topics.ncert_sections: Thinking about Language I and V

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the metaphors in the story and the qualities they compare.
Match names of storms such as hailstorm, tornado and gale with their descriptions.

chapters.title: Nelson Mandela: Long Walk to Freedom

topics.title: The inauguration at the Union Buildings and Mandela's address

concepts.learning_objective: Recall the place, people and significance of the inauguration ceremony of 10 May 1994.
Interpret the ideals and references in Mandela's inaugural address.

topics.title: The air show and the two national anthems

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how the generals' salute and the air show showed the military's new loyalty to democracy.
Explain the significance of the two national anthems sung at the inauguration.

topics.title: The legacy of apartheid: character, courage and love

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how decades of oppression produced people of extraordinary character, South Africa's greatest wealth.
State Mandela's view that courage is the triumph over fear, not its absence.
Explain why Mandela believes that love comes more naturally to the human heart than hate.

topics.title: Twin obligations and the growing hunger for freedom

concepts.learning_objective: Describe Mandela's twin obligations and why apartheid made it impossible to fulfil both.
Trace how Mandela's idea of freedom changed from boyhood to manhood.

topics.title: Freedom is indivisible: the oppressor and the oppressed

concepts.learning_objective: Explain Mandela's idea that freedom is indivisible and the chains on one are the chains on all.
Explain why Mandela says the oppressor is a prisoner of hatred who must also be liberated.

topics.title: Language study: noun forms, 'the' with names, idioms and contrasts

concepts.learning_objective: Form nouns from verbs with suffixes such as -ion, -ment and -ance.
Interpret the use of 'the' and the plural with proper nouns to mean people of that kind.
Interpret idiomatic phrases and balanced contrasts in Mandela's prose.

topics.title: His First Flight: the young seagull's fear

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why the young seagull could not bring himself to fly although he was physically able to.
Describe how the seagull's parents and siblings reacted to his refusal to fly.

topics.title: His First Flight: hunger and the mother's plan

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how hunger drove the young seagull to overcome his fear.
Interpret the mother's use of the piece of fish to make the seagull leave the ledge.

topics.title: His First Flight: the first flight and landing on the sea

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the seagull's feelings and movements during his first flight.
Evaluate the ending of the story and the lesson it conveys about overcoming fear.

topics.title: The Black Aeroplane: the night flight and the risk

concepts.learning_objective: Recall the setting and details of the narrator's flight in the Dakota.
Analyse why the narrator chose to fly into the storm and judge that decision.

topics.title: The Black Aeroplane: lost in the storm and the mysterious helper

concepts.learning_objective: Describe what happened to the narrator and his instruments inside the storm clouds.
Interpret the mysterious ending and the role of the black aeroplane.

topics.title: Vocabulary: meanings of 'black' and 'fly', and glossary words

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the meaning of the word 'black' in different contexts.
Use phrases with 'fly' and words with a meaning close to 'fly' correctly.
Recall the meanings of difficult words glossed in the chapter.

chapters.title: From the Diary of Anne Frank

topics.title: Before You Read: Anne Frank and kinds of personal records

concepts.learning_objective: Recall who Anne Frank was, when and why she kept her diary, and why it became famous.
Distinguish a diary, a journal, a log and a memoir by their features.

topics.title: Why Anne keeps a diary and calls it Kitty

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why Anne feels she has no true friend and turns to a diary.
Interpret Anne's decision to treat her diary as a friend named Kitty.

topics.title: A brief sketch of Anne's life

concepts.learning_objective: Recall the main facts of Anne's family and their move from Germany to Holland.
Infer Anne's feelings for her grandmother and her teacher Mrs Kuperus.

topics.title: The class meeting and Mr Keesing's essays

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the class's anxiety about the meeting that decides promotion.
Recall the three essays Mr Keesing set and how Anne answered each.
Evaluate what the chatterbox episode reveals about Anne and Mr Keesing.

topics.title: Language study: compound words, phrasal verbs, idioms and contracted forms

concepts.learning_objective: Identify compound words from the lesson and the part of speech they form.
Work out the meanings of phrasal verbs and idioms used in the lesson.
Expand contracted forms correctly and explain their use in diary language.

topics.title: A Baker from Goa: the pader and the author's childhood memories
topics.ncert_sections: Part I, 'A Baker from Goa' (opening and childhood memories)

concepts.learning_objective: Students will explain how the traditional Goan baker, the pader, still carries on the craft of bread-making.
Students will describe the baker's daily visits and why the children eagerly ran to meet him.
Students will identify the nostalgic and humorous tone of the author's recollections.

topics.title: A Baker from Goa: bread in Goan life, the baker's dress and prosperity
topics.ncert_sections: Part I, 'A Baker from Goa' (bread in Goan life, the kabai, accounts and prosperity)

concepts.learning_objective: Students will relate bread items such as the bol, cakes and bolinhas to Goan occasions and festivals.
Students will describe the baker's dress in Portuguese days and in the author's childhood.
Students will interpret how the baker collected his bills and why baking was considered profitable.

topics.title: Coorg: the land and its people
topics.ncert_sections: Part II, 'Coorg' (location, climate, the Kodavus and their traditions)

concepts.learning_objective: Students will state the location, landscape and best season to visit Coorg.
Students will explain the Greek and Arab theories about the origin of the Kodavus.
Students will identify evidence of the martial tradition and hospitality of the people of Coorg.

topics.title: Coorg: river, wildlife, adventure and sights
topics.ncert_sections: Part II, 'Coorg' (Kaveri, wildlife, adventure sports, Brahmagiri, Nisargadhama, Bylakuppe)

concepts.learning_objective: Students will describe the river Kaveri and the birds and animals found in Coorg.
Students will explain how Coorg's adventure sports attract even laidback visitors.
Students will identify sights such as the Brahmagiri hills, Nisargadhama and Bylakuppe.

topics.title: Tea from Assam: the journey and the legends of tea
topics.ncert_sections: Part III, 'Tea from Assam' (the train journey, legends and history of tea)

concepts.learning_objective: Students will describe the train journey and the two boys' different reactions to the tea country.
Students will retell the Chinese and Indian legends about the discovery of tea.
Students will recall facts about the early history and spread of tea.

topics.title: Tea from Assam: the Dhekiabari Tea Estate
topics.ncert_sections: Part III, 'Tea from Assam' (arrival at Mariani and the tea estate)

concepts.learning_objective: Students will interpret the description of the tea estate and the work of the tea-pluckers.
Students will explain what the second-flush period is and why it matters.

topics.title: Vocabulary and language work from the chapter
topics.ncert_sections: Glossary; Collocations; compound words; -ing and -ed adjectives

concepts.learning_objective: Students will give the meanings of words glossed in the chapter as used in context.
Students will identify words that commonly go together (collocations).
Students will use verb-particle compound words and -ing/-ed adjectives correctly.

topics.title: Maxwell's plan and the long wait at Basra

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why Maxwell wanted to keep an otter and why he thought Camusfearna suited the experiment.
Recall the events at Basra that delayed Maxwell and led to his getting the otter.

topics.title: Mijbil's arrival, naming and early days

concepts.learning_objective: Describe Mijbil's appearance and early behaviour, and why his species was named Maxwell's otter.
Interpret what Mijbil's behaviour in the bathroom reveals about otters and water.
Analyse how Maxwell's description of Mij's play shows the otter's skill and intelligence.

topics.title: The journey from Basra: the box and the aircraft

concepts.learning_objective: Recall the arrangements Maxwell had to make to fly Mij from Basra to London.
Interpret Mij's struggle in the box and Maxwell's rush to the airport.
Evaluate the events on the aircraft and the role of the air hostess.

topics.title: Mij in London: games, walks and Londoners' guesses

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the game Mij invented with the ping-pong ball and the damaged suitcase.
Explain Mij's compulsive habits on walks and how Maxwell compares them to children's rituals.
Analyse the Londoners' guesses about Mij and the humour in Maxwell's account of them.

topics.title: Language work: would and used to, noun modifiers, quantity phrases
topics.ncert_sections: Thinking about Language I, II, III

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish the use of would and used to for repeated past actions and past states.
Identify nouns, proper nouns and adjectives used as modifiers before a noun.
Use phrases such as a cloud of and a gust of to express quantities of uncountable nouns.

topics.title: Valli's fascination with the bus and her secret plan

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how Valli's curiosity about the street and the bus grew into an overwhelming desire to ride it.
Describe how Valli gathered the facts of the journey and used them to plan a return trip.

topics.title: Boarding the bus: the conductor and the passengers

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why the jolly conductor teases Valli by calling her 'madam'.
Analyse how Valli insists on being treated as a grown-up by the conductor and the passengers.

topics.title: Saving the fare and the journey to town

concepts.learning_objective: Describe how Valli saved sixty paise and resisted temptations to do so.
Recall the sights Valli enjoyed on the way to town, including the running cow.
Explain why Valli stayed on the bus in town and refused the conductor's offer of a drink.

topics.title: The return journey and the dead cow

concepts.learning_objective: Interpret how the sight of the dead cow introduces Valli to the reality of death.
Explain how Valli's mood and behaviour change on the return journey.

topics.title: Coming home: knowing and understanding

concepts.learning_objective: Describe how Valli returns home and keeps her journey a secret from the grown-ups.
Interpret the mother's remark about knowing and understanding in the light of Valli's day.

topics.title: Valli's character, the child's point of view and vocabulary

concepts.learning_objective: Identify Valli's character traits from her words and actions.
Recognise how the story presents sights from an eight-year-old's point of view.
Use the meanings of words glossed in the story.

topics.title: Poem: The Tale of Custard the Dragon (Ogden Nash)

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how the 'cowardly' Custard proves the bravest when the pirate attacks.
Identify the ballad form, humour and poetic devices used in the poem.

topics.title: Siddhartha's search for enlightenment

concepts.learning_objective: Recall how the sights of sickness, age, death and a begging monk led Prince Siddhartha to seek enlightenment.
Explain how Siddhartha became the Buddha and where he preached his first sermon.

topics.title: Kisa Gotami's grief and the mustard-seed task

concepts.learning_objective: Describe Kisa Gotami's first search for medicine and how her neighbours reacted.
Explain the condition the Buddha set for the mustard-seed and the purpose behind it.

topics.title: Kisa Gotami's realisation

concepts.learning_objective: Interpret the image of the flickering city lights as a symbol of human life.
Explain why Kisa Gotami calls herself selfish in her grief and what she comes to understand.

topics.title: The Buddha's sermon on death and grief

concepts.learning_objective: Interpret the similes the Buddha uses to show that all mortals are subject to death.
Explain why the Buddha says lamentation brings no peace and how peace of mind is obtained.

topics.title: Language and style of the text

concepts.learning_objective: Rephrase the old-fashioned words and expressions of the text in current English.
Explain how semicolons join closely related clauses and split such a sentence into simple sentences.
Recall the meanings of key words glossed in the chapter.

topics.title: Grief in modern texts compared with the sermon

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the feelings of grief and the ways of helping a grieving person described in the guide.
Compare Amitai Etzioni's experience of grief in 'Good Grief' with the Buddha's teaching.

topics.title: The playwright, the genre and the theme of the play

concepts.learning_objective: Students will identify Anton Chekhov as the author and explain why the play is a one-act farce.
Students will explain the play's theme of wealthy families seeking marriages that make economic sense.

topics.title: Lomov's arrival and Chubukov's response to the proposal

concepts.learning_objective: Students will analyse how Chubukov's asides and later conduct reveal the insincerity of his affection for Lomov.
Students will describe how Lomov's dress and nervous behaviour reveal his anxiety about proposing.

topics.title: Lomov's soliloquy: his reasons for marrying and his health

concepts.learning_objective: Students will explain the practical reasons for which Lomov decides to marry Natalya.
Students will identify the ailments Lomov complains of and how they make him a comic figure.

topics.title: The quarrel over Oxen Meadows
topics.ncert_sections: Lomov and Natalya; Chubukov joins the quarrel

concepts.learning_objective: Students will explain each side's claim to Oxen Meadows and why the dispute is petty.
Students will analyse how pride and family insults turn the dispute into an absurd quarrel.

topics.title: The quarrel over Guess and Squeezer, and the ending
topics.ncert_sections: Lomov's return; the dogs; the engagement

concepts.learning_objective: Students will recall the details and arguments of the quarrel over the dogs Guess and Squeezer.
Students will interpret the ironic ending in which the engaged couple go on quarrelling.

topics.title: Language: reported speech, phrases and translated expressions
topics.ncert_sections: Thinking about Language I, II and III

concepts.learning_objective: Students will convert sentences from the play from direct speech into reported speech.
Students will explain the meaning of phrases from the play such as 'my foot's gone to sleep'.
Students will recognise expressions in the play that reflect its Russian original rather than idiomatic English.
